text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on October 18. Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.

- Vice president Godfrey Miyanda on Thursday ruled out the possibility of government reversing laws that ban some candidates, including former prersident Kenneth Kaunda, from contesting this years elections.

- Finance minister Ronald Penza said the government was not optimistic about obtaining significant balance of payment support from donors in 1997 and beyond, but said Zambians must take the withdrawal of western aid as a challenge.

- Vice president Godfrey Muiyanda said on Thursday opposition parties were deliberately creating conditions to force the government to introduce a state of emergency. Miyanda told Parliament that the government would be forced to introduce a state of mergency if the opposition continued to incite people to violence.

- The Commonwealth Press Union has warned the government against harrassing Fred Mmembe, editor of the independent newspaper, The Post. Mmembe, who this week won a Commonwealth press award, told reporters in South Africa that the government intended to arrest him for criticising it in his acceptance speech.
